summary: Guided quiet-fallback and validation for retracting aggressive prefetch/batch/quant profiles
description: Issue summary: Customer reports increased 5xx errors and occasional accuracy regressions after enabling an aggressive combined profile (async_batching=on, kv_prefetch=enabled, quant_profile=4bit-aggressive) on Dedicated capacity. Impact: Intermittent user-facing timeouts and degraded prompt completions for a production tenant; traffic is large-scale (steady 9k qps). Environment: prod-us-west (dedicated pool), tenant: nimbus-prod. Observed: spike in server 5xx and token tail-latency starting ~2026-03-13 08:20 UTC after profile rollout window. Customer requested assisted rollback and validation checklist to avoid service disruption and semantic regressions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant traffic routed to dedicated pool in prod-us-west. 2) Apply optimizer profile: async_batch=true, kv_prefetch=on, quant_profile='4bit-aggressive' via config-service. 3) Run long-running multi-turn chat sessions and prompt-heavy evaluation harness (10k requests over 10 mins, mixed seq lengths). 4) Observe 5xx errors and token-latency spikes in serving runtime and increased model output entropy.

comments: 2026-03-13T09:05:00Z - Maya Lee (Support): Acknowledged report, opened P1 support ticket. Requested immediate telemetry (top 5 traces, liveness, eviction stats) and whether tenant has session affinity.
2026-03-13T09:22:37Z - NimbusLabs (Customer): Confirmed profile rollout at 08:15 UTC. Provided short traces and told there were spikes in completion entropy and some aborted streams.

2026-03-13T10:10:12Z - Carlos Rivera (SRE): Initial hypothesis: combined aggressive quant + kv-prefetch is causing memory compaction and increased cache churn leading to batch serialization timeouts. Requested PRAGMA: temporarily disable kv_prefetch per-tenant and observe for 30m.

2026-03-13T10:58:44Z - NimbusLabs (Customer): Applied temporary kv_prefetch=false via console. Early results: 5xx rate reduced but small latency increase on median tokens. Asked for safe revert plan for full rollback.

2026-03-13T11:30:00Z - Carlos Rivera (SRE): Recommended staged rollback: 1) Snapshot current optimizer config for tenant, 2) apply per-tenant snapshot restore to previous stable profile, 3) run canary traffic at 5% for 10 minutes, 4) promote if stable. Posting detailed checklist below.
2026-03-13T14:05:12Z - Maya Lee (Support): Preparing runbook and will coordinate with CS for communication window and verification tests.
investigation_notes: Telemetry review: correlation between kv-cache evictions and spikes in batch_wait_ms; memory pressure detected on 3/4 nodes in pool 'dedi-usw'.
Hypothesis A: Aggressive 4-bit quantization combined with async batching increases per-request decode CPU jitter, amplifying contention when KV cache is busy.
Hypothesis B: kv_prefetch introduced additional background IO that competes with runtime kernel launches (observed kernel queue depth growth in perf traces).
Observed mitigations: Disabling kv_prefetch reduced 5xx by ~72% in short A/B test but increased median token latency by ~8ms.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: Customer toggled kv_prefetch=false per-tenant at 2026-03-13T10:58 UTC — immediate reduction in 5xx and evictions observed.

Planned safe rollback (recommended): 1) Create a config snapshot of the current optimizer profile (config-service snapshot create --tenant nimbus-prod --label post-incident). 2) Restore previous stable profile (snapshot restore --tenant nimbus-prod --snapshot stable-2026-03-10) in 'staged' mode without global promotion. 3) Route 5% canary traffic using traffic-split API for 10 minutes while running verification prompts (provided test-suite). 4) If canary stable (no 5xx, latency within 95p baseline, semantic pass rate >98%), promote to 100% during low-traffic window. 5) If regressions observed, restore snapshot again and open escalation to runtime team.

Validation checklist (required before promote): run the provided eval set (50 multi-turn chat sessions), confirm KV eviction rate < baseline+5%, 95p latency not increased by >10%, and semantic similarity delta < 0.02 for generation outputs.

Follow-ups: Create a short RFC to add an automatic safety gate that prevents combined application of '4bit-aggressive' quant_profile with kv_prefetch=true on the same tenant without explicit SRE approval. Owner: Carlos Rivera.
next_steps: Coordinate 30-min maintenance window with NimbusLabs for full rollback and promotion (CS to schedule).
SRE to prepare snapshot restore playbook and execute canary on demand.
Support to run the validation suite and collect pre/post metrics for 1 hour post-promotion.
Engineering to draft safety gate RFC to prevent risky optimizer profile combinations; target review by 2026-03-20.
